# Neuroscience App

A browse-first neuroscience reading app for two audiences — newcomers building
foundations, and researchers/clinicians tracking the frontier.

## Core principle: nothing is generated by the app

All content is **fetched live from cited sources at runtime**. The app never
authors, paraphrases-to-distortion, or invents neuroscience facts. Where a
source has no matching content, a section shows **“No referenced content
available”** rather than filling the gap.

- **Article text** — English **Wikipedia** (REST + Action API), shown verbatim
  with a link back to the exact source section. Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA;
  attribution is surfaced on every page.
- **Studies & experiments** — **Europe PMC** API: real peer-reviewed papers
  with authors, journal, year, and a link to the source.

## Structure

Six primary browse categories (see `src/data/taxonomy.js`):

1. **Anatomy / Structure** — 20 topics (cortex, limbic system, basal ganglia, …)
2. **Level of Analysis / Scale** — the classic spine: molecular → cellular →
   synaptic → circuit → systems → cognitive → behavioural → social
3. **Functions** — memory, attention, consciousness, …
4. **Disorders / Clinical** — grouped: neurodegenerative, psychiatric,
   developmental, injury & other
5. **Neurochemistry / Signalling** — dopamine, serotonin, glutamate/GABA, …
6. **Lifespan / Development** — neurodevelopment, plasticity, ageing, …

Each topic page draws out, where the source provides it: overview, what it
looks like in the brain, history & discovery, what we’ve learned, treatments,
current challenges, open questions, and the studies/scientists behind it.

`taxonomy.js` contains **no facts** — only the browse structure and, per topic,
*where* to fetch (Wikipedia title + literature search query).

## Run

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:5173
```

Requires Node (this repo was developed on v24 via nvm). The app is fully
client-side; the Wikipedia and Europe PMC APIs are CORS-enabled, so no backend
or API key is needed.

## Project layout

```
src/
  data/taxonomy.js         # browse structure + fetch targets (no facts)
  api/wikipedia.js         # overview + section fetch & heading->bucket mapping
  api/literature.js        # Europe PMC study search
  components/TopicPage.jsx # live-fetch topic page (sourced sections + studies)
  App.jsx                  # sidebar, home, category/spine/group views, routing
  styles.css
```

## Not yet built

- Persisted/bookmarkable URLs (routing is in-memory state today).
